S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 48 hours of learning of it, with a follow-up investigation report within 30 days. Affected customers must be notified promptly when an incident indicates a potential safety risk, and no later than five days after that determination.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, fire, injury, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 48 hours of learning of it, with a follow-up investigation report within 30 days. Affected customers must be notified promptly when an incident indicates a potential safety risk, and no later than five days after that determination. Reports shall include incident counts, installed-unit denominators, model, known harms, and corrective actions. Manufacturers shall retain records and report incidents even when the cause is uncertain.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. A result above 5% triggers regulator review and a corrective-action plan; any sales restriction shall be determined by the regulator based on evidence and risk.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. Manufacturers shall submit per-model test methods, sample sizes, and results to the regulator before sale and after any material design change. Customers considering or owning a model shall receive its individual 55 °C failure rate, test date, a plain-language summary of its safety status, clear safety instructions, and any required actions. A result above 5% triggers regulator review and a corrective-action plan; any sales restriction shall be determined by the regulator based on evidence and risk. The parties will review the threshold against accumulated evidence after two years.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New home battery units placed on the market from 24 months after adoption shall support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent safe alternative within six years, prioritizing units with elevated risk.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New home battery units placed on the market from 24 months after adoption shall support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. For units already installed on the adoption date, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent safe alternative within six years, prioritizing units with elevated risk. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers of the capability, limitations, and any required action.

parameters.quote: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New home battery units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption of this standard. The requirement applies to all models placed on the market from that date; manufacturers shall document the system’s effectiveness and maintenance requirements in the product safety materials.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A model exceeding 8 confirmed thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period shall trigger prompt regulator review of verified counts, denominators, attribution, and risk. The regulator shall determine whether a recall or other corrective action is required based on that evidence.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase and upon material updates, manufacturers shall provide customers with clear safety instructions, a plain-language summary of the applicable model’s safety status, and any required customer actions. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks, corrective actions, and any recall, using direct contact where reasonably available and public notice otherwise. A model exceeding 8 confirmed thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period shall trigger prompt regulator review of verified counts, denominators, attribution, and risk. The regulator shall determine whether a recall or other corrective action is required based on that evidence. Pending review, manufacturers shall promptly notify the regulator and implement interim protections for customers and neighbours where warranted. Review shall not delay necessary interim protections.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s Ember 8 has a 3.9% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test
ground_truth_claims.message_text: Halcyon’s Ember 8 has a 3.9% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test and had 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year. These figures support retaining the 5% test limit. We cannot speak for other models from these figures. Per-model test results should be disclosed to customers of that model as well as submitted to regulators.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Northwind’s Hearth 10 recorded a 6.2% failure rate at 55 °C
ground_truth_claims.message_text: Northwind’s Hearth 10 recorded a 6.2% failure rate at 55 °C and 6.4 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year. We support confidential submission of per-model results to regulators, but not disclosure of individual failure rates to customers. A fixed 5% cutoff with automatic market exclusion is not justified without a review process and evidence-based corrective action. Our proposed text preserves regulator oversight while allowing review of the threshold.

judge_section_notes: S1 is strict: all incidents reported within 48h, records kept, reporting even when cause uncertain, customer notice within 5 days. S2 sets a 55°C test and 5% review threshold but does not mandate sales stop above 5%, and gives customers individual failure rates without public publication. S3 requires new-unit shut-off from 24 months and retrofit within six years. S4 requires built-in suppression from 36 months. S5 uses an 8/100k review trigger but leaves recall to regulator discretion, with prompt customer notices.
